info.title: TorqueLane API
info.description: TorqueLane API. Errors always use the envelope { "error": { "code", "message", "details"? } }; clients branch on `code`. Records outside the tenant scope of the caller answer 404 not_found, exactly like records that do not exist.

servers.description: Relative to the environment host, e.g. https://api-staging.<domain>

get.description:
`ledger:view` (staff). Every account with its balance through `as_of`
(default today) over the caller's branches, and the posting rules that
point at it. The chart is installed on first use.

post.description:
`ledger:manage`. A new account takes no postings until a posting rule
is pointed at it. Its code is unique in the chart.

patch.description:
`ledger:manage`. Rename or describe it, or deactivate one no posting
rule uses. Once an account has been posted to its code, type and side
are fixed (409).

get.description:
`ledger:view`. Each event or category the books post by, the account it
posts to and the account type it needs.

put.description:
`ledger:manage`. Re-point rules at other accounts of the right type.
It applies to postings from now on; entries already made are never
rewritten.

get.description:
`ledger:view`. The accounting product the books are exported for
(`none`, `xero` or `quickbooks`) and the account mappings its import
needs.

put.description:
`ledger:manage`. `xero` and `quickbooks` switch on that product's
manual-journal import file next to the plain CSV.

`ledger:manage`. Our account → the code (Xero) or name (QuickBooks
Online) the accountant's books use; an empty code and name removes the
mapping.

get.description:
Most severe first, then most urgent. PMS alerts only where repair_pms
is active. Ids are deterministic (`pms:<vehicle>:<task>`,
`doc:<document>`, `licence:<vehicle>`, …). `?include_dismissed=1` adds
dismissed ones (flagged).

The fleet overview in one call: the fleet summary, overdue and
due-soon demand (`serviceDemand`), 30-day rolling spend, twelve months
of closed cost, the six-week upcoming load, stale odometers, expiring
documents, the three most urgent items, and the next five active work
orders by scheduled date.

Every tracked interval across the fleet, most urgent first
(`compareUrgency`), grouped by lead time: overdue, next 7, next 30 and
next 90 days (each with its catalogue cost). `status` (ok | due_soon |
overdue) filters the rows; the six-week load and the demand bands are
always the whole fleet's, the same figures the dashboard shows.

Over the last `months` (3, 6 or 12; default 12) of closed work: monthly
cost and maintenance mix, total and preventive share of spend, cost per
fleet kilometre (distance driven IN the period, from each vehicle's
daily average), mean days between services, and the rankings: costliest
vehicles, spend by service item, services per 10,000 km.

cost_per_km_cents.description: Centavos per km driven in the period, rounded once (half up).

get.description:
What "Auto-schedule overdue" would book: every overdue item no live
work order covers, worst first, from tomorrow at three a day (critical
tasks as critical, the rest high), each with its estimate (catalogue
parts + hours at the shop rate), and the total. Accounts that take no
new work are left out. `POST /work-orders/auto-schedule` books exactly
this, recomputed. `can_commit`: the caller holds `workorder:create`.

The approvals queue (../web's Requests screen): quotations pending
approval, oldest first, each with its pending value, business hours
waited against its own SLA, and whether the caller may decide it; what
waits on the caller; approved work not yet booked; spend committed
this Manila month against the scope's monthly budget; and the mean
approval turnaround. Every order is judged against its OWN effective
settings. Staff may narrow to one `customer_account_id`. Needs
repair_pms.

Staff. The organization's defaults, the selected branch's override
(X-Branch-Id) and what that branch runs on.

put.description: `organization:manage`.
`settings:manage` in that branch. A null field inherits the organization's.

get.description:
The account's sparse overrides and the settings they resolve to (for
staff, in the selected branch). Anyone who can see the account; a
portal user's own.
`ledger:view`. Newest statement first.

post.description:
`ledger:manage`. `account_id` (a cash, bank, wallet or clearing
account), `statement_date`, `statement_balance_cents` (the statement's
closing balance; negative when overdrawn). One open at a time per

get.description:
The statement against the books: what cleared on earlier statements,
what is ticked on this one, the difference still to explain, what is
outstanding, and every line the statement could show.

`ledger:manage`. `clear`: journal line ids the statement shows;
`unclear`: ids ticked by mistake. A line clears once, ever.

post.description:
`ledger:manage`. Only when the statement balance equals everything
cleared (409 `statement_does_not_agree` otherwise, with the

`settings:manage` and access to `branch_id`.

get.description:
Exact match on the normalised plate (case, spaces, dashes ignored), then
the VIN, over the vehicles the caller may see. Under 3 characters the
outcome is `idle`; no match is `new` (a 17-character entry is taken as
a VIN). A stale odometer is never pre-filled: `form.odometer` is null
and `form.odometer_needs_confirmation` true, with the last reading in
`last_odometer` for reference.

Staff with `customer:manage` and `vehicle:manage`. One transaction:

granted), and the vehicle with the reading taken at the counter.
post.summary: Register a new customer and vehicle at the counter

post.description:
`customer:manage`. Staff record how the customer told them (in person,
paper form, email, SMS, phone); a portal user records their own through
the `portal` channel. Allowed on a suspended account.

get.description:
`billing:view`. Newest first; `status` `issued` or `void`,
`customer_account_id`, `branch_id`, `invoice_id`.

post.description:
`billing:void` (staff); requires an `Idempotency-Key`. `reason`,
`issued_on` (default today), and `lines`: an `invoice_line_id` alone
credits what is left of that line; with `quantity`, that many at the
line's price; with `unit_price_cents`, that amount. A line with no
`invoice_line_id` is an allowance (`description`, `unit_price_cents`).
The notes on an invoice never exceed what it billed.

The note comes off the invoice's balance as far as the invoice still
owed (`applied_cents`); the rest is the customer's credit
(`credit_cents`), paid out by a refund. Books Dr Sales Returns &
Allowances, Dr Output VAT / Cr Accounts Receivable, Cr Customer
Deposits.

`billing:void`, with a reason. Only while none of its credit has been
refunded. The invoice owes again what the note had taken off it.

The staff a task or a lead can be given to, the pipeline's stages, and
the lists the forms offer.

what the CRM knows of each: what they have paid, when they were last

`crm:view`. What to tell the customer at the counter: the tier they
hold and what it gives, the prepaid packages they can still use, and
their points.

post.description: `crm:work`.

put.description: `crm:work`. Its text, or whether it is pinned.

post.description: `crm:work`. Whatever membership they held ends as this one starts.

post.description:
`crm:work`. `points` is signed: negative for points the customer spent
(`redeemed`), either way for a correction (`adjusted`). A balance never
goes below zero (409).

get.description: `crm:view`. With how many customers hold each.

post.description: `crm:manage`. A discount (0–100%), priority booking, and the detailing add-ons a member gets free.

put.description: `crm:manage`. Only what is sent changes.

get.description: `crm:view`.

post.description:
`crm:manage`. So many credits for a price; a credit pays for one
detailing job (of `detailing_package_id`, or of any package when null).

put.description: `crm:manage`. Packages already sold keep what they were sold as.

get.description:
`crm:view`. Newest first; `customer_account_id` for one customer's.
`summary.unearned_cents` is what is still owed as service across them
all: what Unearned Revenue should hold for prepaid packages.

post.description:
`crm:work`. Numbered and booked in one transaction: Dr the cash-side
account of `payment_method` / Cr Unearned Revenue. `branch_id` is the
branch that took the money (the session's branch when not given).
Needs an `Idempotency-Key`.

vat_cents.description: The VAT inside the price, charged when it was sold; the rest is what its credits earn.

unearned_cents.description: What is still owed as service: this package's share of Unearned Revenue.

post.description:
`crm:work`. One credit of the package settles a finished, signed-off
detailing job of the same customer (`detailing_booking_id`), which then
cannot be invoiced. Books Dr Unearned Revenue / Cr Sales – Detailing
for the credit's share of the price. Refused with 409 and a `reason`
(`not_billable`, `wrong_package`, `no_credits`, `expired`,
`already_settled`). Needs an `Idempotency-Key`.

get.description:
Quiet hours (minutes of the Manila day), the reminder cooldown, when a
customer counts as lapsed, the campaign hourly limit, and whether
feedback and loyalty points are on.

put.description: `crm:manage`. Only what is sent changes.

get.description: `crm:view`. With the placeholders each uses, and the lists the form offers.

post.description: `crm:manage`.

put.description: `crm:manage`. A template a rule or a campaign uses keeps its purpose (409).

delete.description: `crm:manage`. Only one that was never used; switch a used one off instead (409).

get.description:
`crm:view`. The four kinds of service reminder, each with its rule
(`null` until one is set).

put.description:
`crm:manage`. Whether this kind of reminder is sent, with which
service-reminder template, and (for documents) how many days ahead.

post.description:
`crm:manage`. The run the schedule makes every morning: candidates from
the maintenance engine, detailing repeat intervals, document expiries
and lapsed customers; each held to consent, opt-out, the cooldown and
quiet hours. Returns how many were queued and why the rest were not.

get.description:
`crm:view`. Everything sent, queued, failed and skipped, newest first.
`status`, `purpose`, `source_type` (+ `source_id`) and
`customer_account_id` narrow it. A skipped message says why
(`skip_reason`: `no_consent`, `opted_out`, `no_address`).

`crm:view`. The organization's Net Promoter Score and the answers
behind it, newest first.

`crm:view`. Open tasks first, the soonest due at the top. `status`
(`open`, `done`, `cancelled`, or `all`; default `open`), `mine` for the
caller's own, `customer_account_id` or `lead_id` for one subject's.
`summary` counts the open ones: overdue, due today, with a reminder due.

post.description:
`crm:work`. About a customer or a lead; with an assignee, a due date and
a reminder time when wanted.

put.description: `crm:work`. Only what is sent changes; a reminder moved to a new time is due again.

post.description: `crm:work`. `status`: `done`, `cancelled` or `open`.
post.summary: Finish, cancel or re-open a task

get.description:
`crm:view`. Every lead, grouped by stage in board order, with each
stage's count and value, and the open pipeline's total.

post.description: `crm:work`. It starts in `new`, owned by whoever adds it unless an owner is named.

get.description: With its tasks.

put.description: `crm:work`. Its own fields; the stage moves through its own action. A won lead is closed to edits (409).

post.description:
`crm:work`. Between the open stages freely; to `lost` with a
`lost_reason`; a lost lead may be re-opened. `won` is refused here (409
`convert_to_win`): a lead is won by converting it.
post.summary: Move a lead to another stage

post.description:
`crm:work`. Creates a company account with the terms and approval
overrides given, tagged `dealer` when the lead was one, and records the
customer's consent (`consent_channel` says how it was given;
`service_reminders` and `marketing` only when they agreed to them). The
lead becomes `won` and its tasks move to the account.
post.summary: Win a lead: convert it to a customer account

post.description:
Staff with `customer:manage`. `consents` must include `service_records`,
granted; it is recorded in the same transaction as the account.

put.description:
`customer:manage`. Portal users may edit only their own account's
contact details and branding.

post.description:
Staff with `settings:manage`. The account's portal users are locked out
at once and it takes no new work; staff can still read it.
Staff with `settings:manage`.

get.description:
One customer account's projected spare-parts demand over
`horizon_weeks` (default 6; ../web `computePartsDemand`): its vehicles'
PMS items falling due, less what live work orders and open purchase
orders already cover, against the account's own stock. Rows rank by
shortfall, then quantity required. `summary` is the frontend's
sentence; `can_raise` says whether the caller may turn rows into
purchase requests (`po:issue`, and the account takes new work). Needs
repair_pms.

`from`/`to` (default today, at most 31 days): every booking that sits
on those days, the bays and detailers to lay them out by, the blocked
slots, and how many heads each slot holds against the pool.

The confirmed, on-going and completed jobs that sit on `date` (default
today), as the wall screen shows them.

start_minutes.description: Where it sits on THIS day (a continuation day starts at opening), for sorting and the clock.

get.description:
`package_id`, `size_class`, `date`: every grid slot as a start, whether
it is free and why not (`blocked`, `capacity`, `overflow`), the days
the job would take, when it would end, and which detailers are already
busy in those hours. `start_time` answers for that one time instead
(it need not be on the grid); `except_booking_id` leaves a booking out
when re-timing it.

The branch's realtime channel and what a browser needs to join it.
`enabled: false` means no realtime server is configured: read again
every `poll_seconds`.

post.description:
`detailing:view` in the channel's branch. Signs `socket_id` onto
`channel_name` (`private-detailing.branch.{id}`).

get.description:
`detailing:view`. Newest day first, over the detailing branches the
session works in (`branch_id` narrows it). `meta.summary` counts the
same filters by status and says what today holds.

post.description:
`detailing:book` in the branch. The API plans the days (a job that does
not fit before closing rolls into the next morning), prices the package
for the vehicle's size, and reserves the detailers. A slot that has
filled, a blocked slot or a detailer already on another job is 409 with
`details.reason` (`full`, `blocked`, `detailer_conflict`). The booking
is numbered from the `detailing_booking` series (BK-).

get.description: With its status log.

patch.description: `detailing:book`. Its bay, notes, contact details and vehicle.

post.description:
Starting (`on_going`) and completing need `detailing:work` or
`detailing:book`; every other move `detailing:book`. Any status may
follow any other. Starting needs the check-in inspection (409,
`details.reason` = `inspection_required`) unless
`inspection_override_reason` is given. Completing releases the slots
the job no longer needs and takes its materials from stock, once.

put.description:
`detailing:book`. Checked across the booking's whole span; the heads
reserved follow the names.

`detailing:book`. The whole list; a listed add-on is priced for the
booking's size unless a price is typed.

post.description: `detailing:work`.

`detailing:qc`, on a completed job, by someone other than a detailer
named on it (403 otherwise). `passed: false` needs `notes`.

`detailing:work`. One per stage (`check_in`, `check_out`); sending a
stage again replaces it and, when `damage_points` is sent, its map. A
`mileage` is recorded as an odometer reading of the booking's vehicle:
an implausible one is 422 until sent again with `confirm_mileage`.
`detailing:work`. Multipart; an image, `phase` `before` or `after`.

`detailing:book` and `billing:manage`. A draft invoice for a completed,
signed-off job: the package at the price it was booked at, and each
extra as a line. A booking is invoiced once (409 otherwise).

`detailing:book` and `billing:manage`. Invoice and payment in one
action: raises the invoice if there is none, issues it, and records the
payment against it, all or nothing. Requires an `Idempotency-Key`.
post.summary: Check a booking out at the counter

get.description:
Categories, packages (with prices and materials) and add-ons of the
branch, in their set order, with the branch's detailers. Inactive ones
only with `include_inactive=1`.

How the API reads a typed duration (`text`): slots, minutes, days and
the "Interpreted as …" line, so a typo is caught before it is saved.

put.description: `kind` is `packages`, `categories` or `addons`; `ids` in the order wanted.

The whole package: its prices are replaced by the list sent, and its
materials too when `materials` is sent.

`detailing:view`. A branch that has saved none yet shows the defaults
(`saved: false`).

`detailing:manage`. Only what is sent changes. The pool cannot drop
below what existing bookings already hold in one slot, and a booking
takes no more than the pool by default (422).

post.description:
`detailing:manage`. Closes grid slots of a day to new bookings;
bookings already there stay.

`detailing:manage`. The tokens of the branch's wall screens, revoked

post.description: `detailing:manage`. A preference the shop books from; it books nothing itself.

Today's confirmed, on-going and completed jobs of the token's branch
(Asia/Manila), the branch's name and look, and how to listen for
changes (`realtime`; when it is not enabled, read again every
`poll_seconds`).

branch channel.

The documents screen's tiles under the list's filters: how many, their
total size in bytes, and how many expire within the 45-day warning
window (already expired included).

`document:upload`, multipart. With `vehicle_id` the document is filed
under the vehicle's current owner; otherwise under `customer_account_id`.
Only renewal kinds (registration, CTPL, comprehensive insurance,
emission test, LTFRB franchise, warranty) take `expires_on`. Up to

A short-lived (60 s) URL to the file, issued after the policy check.
409 for a record with no file (imported paper records).

Streams a document's file. Reachable only through the signed, 60-second
URL from GET /documents/{id}/download: the signature (bound to the
document id and expiry, checked by the `signed` middleware) is the
credential, so there is no session and the lookup runs in the named
system context "signed document download".

`equipment:view`. Every tool of the branch with its report (service
status, forecast, life, reliability, utilisation, health) and the floor
in numbers (`summary`).

post.description: `equipment:manage`.

get.description:
Categories, statuses, condition ratings, meter types and service kinds
with their labels, the starting values each category suggests, and the
thresholds the monitor works to.

maintenance_task.const: Oil change, drain tank, replace air filter

get.description:
`equipment:view`. Which tools each detailing package puts hours on,
and how many per completed job.

put.description:
`equipment:manage`. The whole list for one package: `lines` of
`equipment_id` and `hours_per_job`.

get.description: Its report, its usage log and its service history.

put.description: `equipment:manage`. Only what is sent changes.

`equipment:manage`. Only one with nothing logged against it and no
package mapped; any other is 409: retire it instead.

get.description:
Portal users see their account's parts; staff every account's (narrow
with `customer_account_id`). Active parts only unless
`include_inactive`. Needs repair_pms.

post.description:
`settings:manage`. Staff name the `customer_account_id`; a portal
user's part goes to their own account. `current_stock` is the opening
count; afterwards stock changes only by receiving a purchase order.

`settings:manage`. Stock and account cannot change here. `usages`, when
sent, replaces the part's task links.

Only a part never ordered; one on a purchase order answers 409 (set
`is_active: false` instead).

get.description:
The dashboard KPIs over the caller's vehicles (staff may narrow to one
`customer_account_id`), the expiring-documents tile and the thresholds
behind them. Needs repair_pms.
`inventory:view`. Newest first; `status` is `posted` or `voided`.

post.description:
`inventory:manage`, with a reason. The receipt stays on record, marked
void; every move it made is undone by a compensating `return` move, and
the purchase order's status follows. Under a branch that blocks
negative stock this is refused if the goods have already been used.

get.description:
Database and queue status, for uptime monitors. `degraded` (queue
heartbeat missing or older than five minutes) still answers 200; an
unreachable database answers 503 in the error envelope, with the report
under `details.health`.

message.const: The API cannot reach its database.

get.description: `access:manage`.

post.description:
`access:manage`. Portal roles must name an active `customer_account_id`;
staff roles must not name one. You can only invite to roles whose grants
you hold, and a branch-pinned manager only into their own branches.
The invitation link is emailed; the token is never returned.

Creates the account from the emailed invitation token and signs the new
user in (when called with a cookie session). Answers with the same body
as `GET /me`. Rate-limited.

get.description:
`billing:view`. Drafts first, then newest issued. `status`: `draft`,
`issued`, `partially_paid`, `paid`, `void`, or `open` (issued or
partially paid) / `overdue` (open and past its due date).

post.description:
`billing:manage` (staff). Either `work_order_ids`: closed jobs of ONE
account and ONE branch, not yet invoiced (each approved line is billed
at its STORED approved cost: parts and labour as two lines, then each
job's flat fee); or `customer_account_id` + `lines` (+ `branch_id`) for
a typed-in invoice. Unnumbered until issued. A job already on another
invoice is 409.

patch.description:
`billing:manage`. `notes`; a typed-in invoice's `lines` (the whole
list); `discounts` (`line_id`, `discount_cents`) on any draft. Totals
are recomputed. An issued invoice never changes (409).

delete.description:
`billing:manage`. Only a draft (it has no number); its jobs may be
invoiced again. An issued invoice is voided instead.

post.description:
`billing:manage`; requires an `Idempotency-Key`. Numbers the draft from
the organization's `invoice` series (`INV-YYYY-NNNN`) in this
transaction, freezes who it is from and to and its totals (VAT added or
extracted per the branch), dates it (today, or an earlier `issue_date`
that keeps the series in date order) and sets the due date from the
account's payment terms. Queues `invoice.issued`.

`billing:void`, with a reason. Only an issued invoice nothing has been
paid against (void its payments first). It keeps its number; its jobs
may be invoiced again. Queues `invoice.voided`.

get.description:
`inventory:view`. By SKU; active items unless `include_inactive`. Each
item carries, for every branch the caller may see, its reorder point,
bin, the price that applies there and what is on hand.

post.description:
`inventory:manage`. The SKU (and barcode) are unique in the organization.
A service fee is never stocked.

patch.description:
`inventory:manage`. Once stock has moved in an item its stock unit and
whether it is stocked are fixed. Items are never deleted: set
`is_active` to false.

put.description:
`inventory:manage` in that branch. Reorder point and quantity (stock
units), the bin it is kept in, and a price that overrides the item's
for this branch. Send `null` to clear one.
put.summary: Set an item's settings for a branch

get.description:
`ledger:view`. Entries in the caller's branches, newest first, filtered
by date range, account, event, branch, source document or a search on
number, reference and memo.

`ledger:view`. `format` `csv` (default): one row per line. `xero` or
`quickbooks`: that product's manual-journal import, when it is the
organization's accounting target and every account used is mapped
(409 `unmapped_accounts` names the ones that are not). A caller limited
to some branches exports only those branches' lines. No live sync.

Every account with activity through `as_of` (default today), its net
balance in the debit or credit column, and whether the columns agree.

One account's lines over `from`..`to` (default this month) with a
running balance on the account's own side after the balance brought
forward. Paged.

Revenue (net of discounts), cost of sales, gross profit, other expenses
and net profit over `from`..`to`, with a column per branch in scope and
the consolidated total.

Assets, liabilities and equity through `as_of`, including the earnings
made to date; `balanced` says whether assets = liabilities + equity.

By day and branch over `from`..`to`: net sales, VAT and the invoiced
total (voids netted on the day they happened), and the money received
that day by payment method.
`ledger:view`. Newest first, in the caller's branches.

post.description:
`ledger:manage`; requires an `Idempotency-Key`. `memo`, `entry_date`
(default today; never in a closed month), `reference`, and at least two
`lines`: `account_id` with `debit_cents` or `credit_cents`. Debits
equal credits. A control account (receivables, inventory, customer
deposits, payables, GR/IR, unearned revenue) is refused: only its own
documents post to it.

get.description: Its lines are its journal entry's: `GET /ledger/journal?source_id=`.

post.description: `ledger:manage`, with a reason. Posts the mirror entry, dated today.

get.description: Every row, newest first, void rows included.

post.description:
`vehicle:update`. Refused below the current reading (422, the
frontend's message). A reading implying over 3× or under 0.1× the
vehicle's average daily distance is a 422 warning on `value` until
re-sent with `confirm_warning: true`. Not in the future, not dated
before the current reading.

`vehicle:manage`. Appends a correction row; nothing is edited or
deleted. A vehicle keeps at least one effective reading.

get.description:
Every module with its organization switch and, per branch the caller can
reach, the branch switch and whether it is active there. Staff only.

put.description:
Needs `organization:manage`. Switching it off turns it off in every
branch at once.
put.summary: Switch a module for the organization

put.description:
Needs `settings:manage` and access to the branch. Has no effect while
the organization switch is off.
put.summary: Switch a module for a branch

post.description:
Emails a reset link when the address belongs to an account. Answers the
same either way, so it cannot be used to discover accounts.
Rate-limited.
Uses the token from the reset email. Rate-limited.

get.description: `billing:view`. Newest first; `status` `posted` or `void`.

post.description:
`billing:manage` (staff); requires an `Idempotency-Key` (a retry
replays the first answer, never a second payment). `method` cash,
gcash, maya, card, bank_transfer or check (all but cash need
`reference_no`); `amount_cents`; `received_on` (default today, never in
the future). `allocations` (`invoice_id`, `amount_cents`) spread it over
the account's open invoices; without them it goes to the oldest due
first. What is not allocated is the customer's credit. A fully paid
invoice stamps its jobs collected. Queues `payment.received`.

`billing:manage`. Allocates what is left of the payment to open
invoices of its account, as `allocations` says, or oldest due first.

`billing:void`, with a reason. It keeps its number; every invoice it
paid is owed again (and a job it had settled is no longer collected).

get.description:
`ledger:view`. The months that have entries, newest first, with their
status and (once closed) who closed them and the checklist as it
passed. The current month is always listed.

`ledger:view`, `period` `YYYY-MM`. The seven checks for that month
(every source posted; receivables = Accounts Receivable; stock valuation
= Inventory; unapplied credit = Customer Deposits; open vendor bills =
Accounts Payable; unbilled goods receipts = GR/IR Clearing; trial
balance balanced), whether the month can be closed now and, if not, why.
Read-only.

label.const: Every invoice, payment, bill and stock move is posted
Unapplied customer credit equals Customer Deposits
Unbilled goods receipts equal GR/IR Clearing

enum: The month is not over yet.

post.description:
`ledger:manage` (and not branch-limited). Only once the month is over,
earlier months are closed and the checklist passes (409
`close_checklist_failed` carries it). A closed month takes no new entry
and is never reopened; a void of one of its documents posts in the
current month, dated today, naming the original.

label.const: Every invoice, payment, bill and stock move is posted
Unapplied customer credit equals Customer Deposits
Unbilled goods receipts equal GR/IR Clearing

enum: The month is not over yet.

patch.description:
First name, last name (the display `name` becomes "first last") and a
username (letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`; unique in the organization,
case-insensitively; 422 when taken). Answers the refreshed session.

get.description:
The signed-in user, their organization, side, branches (allowed and
selected), customer account (portal), resolved capabilities, active
modules and branding. The frontend gates its UI from this.

put.description:
`current_password` must match (422 otherwise); the new `password`
(with `password_confirmation`) needs 8+ characters and must differ.
Other devices' sessions and remember-me cookies stop working; this
session stays signed in.

get.description:
By the token of its confirmation link: its reference, status, package
and times. An unknown token is 404.

Its name and look (`theme_tokens`), whether online booking is on (and
the notice shown when it is not), the vehicle sizes, and its menu:
every active package with a price per size. `captcha.provider` says
which challenge to draw, if any.

`package_id`, `size_class`, `date`: the times of that day a booking may
start (before closing, not in the past), each free or not, and when the
job would end. Nothing about other bookings.

post.description:
Lands `pending`; the shop confirms it, and the customer is emailed
both times. 409 when the slot has just filled (`details.reason` =
`full`), is blocked, or online booking is off
(`public_booking_disabled`). The `token` opens the confirmation page.

get.description:
What the reminder was about and how to book: the branch's online
booking page (`booking.mode` = `online`), or a booking request the shop
calls back on (`request`).

post.description:
Leaves a booking request on the shop's task list, once per reminder.
`preferred_date` (today or later) and a `note` are optional.

get.description: Whose feedback it is for, and whether it has been given.

post.description: A `score` from 0 to 10 and an optional `comment`. Once: a second answer changes nothing.

get.description: Which shop and which kind of message; whether the address is already opted out.

post.description: Opts the address out of the channel and withdraws consent for that kind of message.

get.description:
Newest first. Portal users see their account's; staff every account's
(narrow with `customer_account_id`); filter by `status`. Needs
repair_pms.

post.description:
`po:issue`. Name the parts to order (`part_ids`) over the horizon the
forecast was read at; the server recomputes the forecast and orders
each part's shortfall at its unit cost, one draft per preferred
vendor. Quantities and prices are never read from the request. A
suspended account takes no new orders (403 account_suspended).
post.summary: Raise purchase requests from the forecast

get.description:
The list's filters as a spreadsheet (`format` xlsx, the default, or
csv): one row per line, ../web `exportPurchaseOrdersToExcel`. Money as
pesos with two decimals. At most 5,000 orders; filter to narrow.

One order, one row per line (../web `exportPurchaseOrderToExcel`),
named after its reference.

post.description:
draft → sent. `po:issue`, and the order's total must sit within the
caller's approval band under the account's settings (403 otherwise,
naming the limit).

sent → received. Each line's quantity goes back into the account's own
stock of that part.
draft or sent → cancelled, with a `reason`. Its number is not reused.

get.description:
`billing:view` (staff). Closed jobs not yet invoiced, oldest finished
first, in the caller's branches; `customer_account_id` narrows it.

`billing:view` (staff). Each account's open balances as of `as_of`
(default today), by days past due: current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, over
90; with the account's unallocated credit. A balance as of a past date
counts only what was issued, paid and voided by then.

`billing:view` (staff). Over `from`..`to` (business dates): invoices
issued and still standing (net sales, VAT, total), and payments received
and still standing (by method).

`billing:view`. What the account owes on open invoices, what is
overdue, its unallocated credit, and where it stands against its credit
limit (`over_limit` warns; new work is never blocked).

`billing:view`. Over `from`..`to` (default the last 30 days): the
balance brought forward, each invoice, payment and void with the running
balance, and the closing balance.

seller.description: What the printed statement carries: who it is from (the organization) and what it is not.

get.description:
`billing:view`. Newest first; `status` `posted` or `void`,
`customer_account_id`, `branch_id`.

post.description:
`billing:void` (staff); requires an `Idempotency-Key`. Exactly one
source: `payment_id` (what that payment has neither allocated nor
already refunded) or `credit_note_id` (the credit that note left over).
`amount_cents` (default: everything the source still holds), `method`
(all but cash need `reference_no`), `refunded_on` (default today),
`reason`. To refund money already applied to an invoice, credit the
invoice first. Books Dr Customer Deposits / Cr the cash-side account of
the method.

`billing:void`, with a reason. It keeps its number, and the credit it
paid out is the customer's again.

get.description: In catalogue order (ties in urgency keep it), inactive ones included.

post.description: Staff with `settings:manage`.

put.description:
Editing an interval never changes any vehicle's recorded service
history; due dates move because they are derived.

delete.description: Only one no vehicle has history for (409 otherwise; deactivate it).

post.description:
Cookie-session login for the SPA: call `GET /sanctum/csrf-cookie` first,
then post with the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header, from an allowed origin. Answers
with the same body as `GET /me`. A session that would resolve to no
tenant scope (a suspended account's portal user, a disabled user) is
refused with its reason. Rate-limited per email and per IP.

Ends the cookie session. Works for any signed-in user, including one
whose account was suspended mid-session.

get.description: Approved or scheduled work booked for `date` (default today).
On the floor now, longest-running first, with minutes elapsed since start.
Closed, not yet collected: outstanding, oldest completion first.

Quotations waiting on the customer, longest wait first, in business
hours (Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 Manila), against each order's SLA.

Booked hours per bay on `date` (catalogue estimates, else labour at
the shop rate, else an hour) against capacity; nothing stops a bay
reading over 100%. `days` adds a trailing daily utilisation series.

Per technician: the job in hand, jobs closed in [`from`, `to`), and mean
actual hours (start → close event) against the estimate.

Recognised on collection, in [`from`, `to`) (default: this month to
date), by customer account and by service item.

The shop home in one call: arriving today, on the floor (elapsed
against the estimate), quotes waiting on the customer (oldest first,
the longest wait in business hours), ready for collection (with the
value on the lot), bay utilisation today, and revenue this week
(Monday start, Manila) against last week. Each order carries its
vehicle and customer name.

value_cents.description: The estimate's labour + parts of every finished job still on the lot.

get.description:
Over the last `months` (3, 6 or 12; default 6), recognised on
collection: revenue by customer and by service item (top 10), approval
turnaround by customer, the maintenance mix by month, and the parts
margin on closed work; plus 21 days of bay utilisation.

Every customer account the shop looks after, biggest spender this
month first: vehicles, open work, mean approval turnaround, revenue
recognised this month (to now), and closed work not yet collected. An
order counts for the account stamped on it at creation.

One customer account from the shop's side: its rollup, its vehicles
(with PMS health where repair_pms is on), its work-order history
(latest first), and its terms: the account, its sparse approval
overrides, and the settings they resolve to.

`inventory:view`. Newest first. `status` is `draft`, `cancelled`, or
one of the derived ones: `issued` (nothing in yet), `partially_received`,
`received`, or `open` (issued or partially received).

post.description:
`inventory:manage` in `branch_id`. A draft, numbered from the
organization's `shop_purchase_order` series (`SPO-…`) in this transaction. Lines are in
the purchase unit (quantity × unit cost, rounded once to a centavo by the
server): a stocked `item_id`, or a line bought for a job
(`work_order_line_id` of a line marked "purchased for job").

patch.description: `inventory:manage`. Only a draft; an issued order's lines never change.

post.description: `inventory:manage`. Sends the draft to the vendor; its lines freeze.

`inventory:manage`, with a reason, while nothing has been received
against it.

`inventory:manage`. Takes in some or all of the outstanding quantity of
an issued order: one numbered goods receipt, and for each stocked line a
`receipt` move into the branch's store (the purchase unit converted to
the stock unit; the average cost moves with it). More than is
outstanding is refused. Partial receipts leave the order
`partially_received`.

get.description:
`inventory:view`. The locations of the branches the caller may see
(each branch has one store).

`inventory:view`. Every item in every location of the selected branch
(or `branch_id`), by SKU: quantity, average cost, value (on hand ×
average, rounded once), the branch's reorder point and bin.
`summary` covers the whole filtered set: its value is summed exactly
and rounded once, so it can differ by a centavo from the rows added up.

`inventory:view`. The stock ledger, newest first, cursor-paged. Filter
by item, location, type, source and Manila business dates (`from`,
`to`). Quantity is signed; `source_reference` is the receipt,
transfer, count or work order behind the move.

`inventory:view`. Derived on read from the balances and each branch's
reorder points; never stored. Worst first: out of stock (critical),
then at or under the reorder point (warning). An alert's id is
`stock:<item>:<location>`.

`inventory:view`. For each active stocked item, per branch: on hand, on
order (issued purchase orders still to arrive), the reorder point and
quantity, and the fleet forecast's shortfall for the same SKU over
`horizon_weeks` (default 6; Phase 4's forecast, per active customer
account). From those: `reason` (`stockout`, `below_reorder_point`,
`forecast_shortfall`) and what to buy, in stock and in purchase units.
Only rows that need something, unless `all`. The forecast is the
fleet's, so it is counted once, against the first branch in scope.

post.description:
`inventory:manage` in the location's branch. The first count of items
in a location, each at a stated cost (an `opening` move). Refused for
an item that already has stock history there: correct it with a stock
count instead.

get.description: `inventory:view`. Newest first; `status` is `open`, `posted` or `cancelled`.

post.description:
`inventory:manage` in the location's branch. Lists the items the books
hold there (and any in `item_ids`), each with what the books say now.
Numbered from the `stock_count` series.

put.description:
`inventory:manage`, while the count is open. A line may carry its own
reason; `counted_quantity: null` un-counts it.

post.description:
`inventory:manage`. Every counted line's variance against what the books
hold now becomes an `adjustment` move carrying a reason (the line's, else
the count's; a variance with neither is refused). Uncounted lines are
left alone.
`inventory:manage`. Only an open sheet; nothing moves.

get.description:
`inventory:view`. Transfers into or out of the branches the caller may
see, newest first.

post.description:
`inventory:manage` in the branch the goods leave. One numbered document:
a `transfer_out` at the source's average cost and a `transfer_in` of the
same quantity and cost at the destination, in one transaction. A source
that would go negative is refused if its branch blocks negative stock.

`inventory:manage` in the branch the goods are now in. A new transfer,
the other way, naming this one. A transfer is reversed at most once, and
a reversal is not itself reversed (make a new transfer).

get.description:
The ATC pick-list (code, usual rate, what it covers). Any well-formed
code is accepted with the rate given: this list is a convenience.

description.const: Purchase of goods by a top withholding agent (corporate supplier)
Purchase of goods by a top withholding agent (individual supplier)
Purchase of services by a top withholding agent (corporate supplier)
Purchase of services by a top withholding agent (individual supplier)
Professional fees (corporate, gross income up to P720,000)
Professional fees (corporate, gross income above P720,000)
Professional fees (individual, gross income up to P3,000,000)
Professional fees (individual, gross income above P3,000,000)

get.description:
Sales by VAT category with output VAT, purchases with input VAT, and
VAT payable (negative: excess input tax). A void or a credit note
counts as a negative on the day it happened. `ledger` is the movement
of the Output and Input VAT accounts over the same period.

One row per customer: sales by VAT category, output VAT, gross.
`file=csv` downloads it.

One row per vendor: purchases by VAT category, input VAT, gross.
`file=csv` downloads it.

Expanded withholding the shop took off vendor bills, one row per
vendor and ATC: the alphalist of payees behind form 1601-EQ.
`file=csv` downloads it.

The 2307s customers handed over, one row per customer and ATC: the
summary alphalist of withholding taxes behind the shop's tax credit.
`file=csv` downloads it.

What BIR form 2307 prints for one vendor and quarter (`year`,
`quarter`; default this quarter): payor, payee, and per ATC the income
payments of each month with the tax withheld. The payor is the branch
selected (`X-Branch-Id`), else the organization.

post.description: `settings:manage` and access to `branch_id`.

put.description:
`access:manage`. Not yourself, and never to or from a role whose grants
you do not hold. `branch_ids: []` means every branch, which only an
unrestricted manager can grant. Roles never move between staff and
portal.

get.description:
`q` matches a plate or VIN on its normalised form ("abc-1234" finds
"ABC 1234"), exactly or as a plate prefix; `search` is a substring of
plate, make, model, driver or location. Filter by `status`,
`customer_account_id`, `department`, and `pms` (ok, due_soon, overdue:
the worst band; stale: odometer over 14 days old). `sort=health` lists
the least healthy first (else by plate).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Plate or VIN, matched on the normalised form (check-in style).

parameters.name: pms
parameters.description: Derived, so evaluated per request: the worst PMS band, or an odometer reading over 14 days old.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Plate, make, model, driver or location, case-insensitive substring.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: plate (the default) or health (least healthy first).

post.description:
`vehicle:manage`. Staff name the `customer_account_id`; a portal user
registers to their own account. Takes the first odometer reading and
any known service history. A suspended account takes no new vehicles
(403 account_suspended).

put.description:
`vehicle:manage`. Never the odometer (POST …/readings) or the owner
(POST …/transfer).

delete.description:
`vehicle:manage`. Vehicles are never deleted: history stays and the
plate becomes free for another vehicle.

post.description:
Staff with `vehicle:manage`. Service history (readings, maintenance
state) stays with the vehicle; documents stay with the account they
were filed under, so the new owner never sees the previous owner's.
The receiving account must be active.

get.description: Staff only (it names other customer accounts).

Every catalogue task evaluated against the vehicle, most urgent first,
with the health score (steep: overdue critical −25, overdue −15,
due-soon critical −8, due-soon −4). Needs repair_pms.
By name.

post.description: `settings:manage`. Names are unique in the organization.

delete.description: Past work orders keep the vendor's name.

get.description:
`payables:view`. Newest first, in the caller's branches. `status`: a
status, or `open` (unpaid or partially paid) or `overdue` (open and past
due); `vendor_id`, `branch_id`, `q` (our number, the vendor's invoice
number, the vendor's name).

post.description:
`payables:manage`; requires an `Idempotency-Key`. `vendor_id`,
`vendor_invoice_no` (once per vendor), `bill_date` (default today),
`due_date` (default: bill date + the vendor's terms),
`prices_include_vat` (default false), `vat_rate_pct` (default 12), and
`lines`: `kind: goods` names a `goods_receipt_line_id` (billed whole,
once; `unit_cost_cents` if the vendor charged other than the receipt's
cost) and `kind: expense` an `account_id`, `description` and
`unit_cost_cents`. `withholding` (`atc_code`, `rate_pct`) withholds
expanded tax on the purchases before VAT; left out, the vendor's usual
code and rate apply; `false` withholds nothing. `payment` (`method`,
`reference_no`) pays the bill in full on the spot.

Books Dr GR/IR (goods on the shelf, at the receipt's value) or the
line's account, Dr Purchase Price Variance, Dr Input VAT / Cr Accounts
Payable, Cr Withholding Tax Payable.

get.description:
`payables:view`. Receipt lines no standing bill has claimed, in the
caller's branches (`vendor_id` narrows it): what a new bill's `goods`
lines can name. `received_value_cents` is what the receipt left in
GR/IR for a line that went on the shelf (null for goods bought for one
job).

post.description:
`payables:manage`, with a reason. Only a bill with nothing paid (void
its payments first). It keeps its number; the books take the mirror
entry, dated today; its receipt lines may be billed again.

get.description:
`payables:view`. Newest first; `status` `posted` or `void`, `method`,
`vendor_id`, `branch_id`, `q` (number or reference).

post.description:
`payables:manage`; requires an `Idempotency-Key`. `method` cash, gcash,
maya, card, bank_transfer or check (all but cash need `reference_no`);
`paid_on` (default today). Either `allocations` (`vendor_bill_id`,
`amount_cents`: the bills it settles) or `amount_cents` alone, spread
over the vendor's open bills at the branch, oldest due first. A payment
settles bills and nothing more: money that pays no bill is refused.
Books Dr Accounts Payable / Cr the cash-side account of the method.

get.summary: Show a payment to a vendor

post.description:
`payables:manage`, with a reason. It keeps its number; every bill it
paid is owed again.
post.summary: Void a payment to a vendor

get.description:
`payables:view`. What each vendor is owed as of `as_of` (default
today), by days past due: current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, over 90. A
balance as of a past date counts only what was billed, paid and voided
by then.

`billing:view`. Newest first; `status` `posted` or `void`,
`customer_account_id`, `branch_id`, `invoice_id`.

post.description:
`billing:manage` (staff). `atc_code` (like WC160), `rate_pct`, and
optionally `tax_base_cents` (default: the invoice's sales before VAT),
`certificate_no`, `received_on` (default today) and the period the
2307 covers (default: the quarter the invoice was issued in). The
amount, round(base × rate / 100), comes off the invoice's balance and
never exceeds it. Books Dr Creditable Withholding Tax / Cr Accounts
Receivable.
post.summary: Record tax withheld from an invoice

post.description: `billing:void`, with a reason. The invoice owes the amount again.

get.description:
Portal users see their account's orders; staff see the organization's,
limited to their branches (a portal request not yet taken into a branch
is visible to all staff). Filter with `status[]`, `stage` (active,
completed, cancelled), `type`, `q` (reference, title, technician,
vendor, plate, customer), `customer_account_id`, `vehicle_id`, `branch_id`,
`technician_id`, `bay_id`, `scheduled_for`; order with `sort` (opened,
the default; scheduled; completed; queue).

post.description:
`workorder:create`. Starts as an unnumbered draft — the number is issued
when it is sent for approval. Lines carry quantities and rates; the
server prices them (any cost or total sent is ignored). Staff raise it
in a branch (`branch_id`, else X-Branch-Id, else their only branch); a
suspended account takes no new work (403 account_suspended). An account
over its credit limit still gets the work: the response adds
`warnings: [{code: credit_limit_exceeded, …}]` and the override is logged.

get.description:
What the list screens total, under the same filters as the list:
orders per bucket (active, completed, cancelled, all) within the scope
filters (`customer_account_id`, `vehicle_id`, `branch_id`), and the
count and value in centavos (labour plus resolved parts) of the fully
filtered set.

post.description:
The check-out panel's "Mark collected": every order in `work_order_ids`
must be closed and not yet collected (409 invalid_transition
otherwise, and none is collected). Staff with `workorder:complete`.

`workorder:create`. Raises one draft per proposal in
`GET /analytics/auto-schedule` (recomputed here, so an item already
covered is never booked twice): the catalogue task as its one line,
scheduled from tomorrow at three a day. Staff narrow with
`customer_account_id` and name the `branch_id` taking the work in (else
X-Branch-Id, else their only repair branch).

patch.description:
`workorder:update`. A declined quote reopens as a draft (it keeps its
number). Any other status is 409.

put.description:
`workorder:update`. The full list: lines with an `id` are updated, new
ones created, missing ones removed. Every cost is recomputed from
quantity × rate on the server.

post.description:
`workorder:update`. Issues the order number. Under the account's
auto-approve ceiling the system approves every line and the order opens
as approved.

`workorder:approve`, within the role's approval band for the pending
amount. Declining a safety-critical line needs a `note`. The order's
status follows from the lines.

Staff, `workorder:update`. Approved work gets a date, a time and a bay
(and optionally a technician); a scheduled order may be re-booked.

`workorder:complete`, while in progress: findings, odometer at service,
parts fitted, tasks discharged.

`workorder:complete`. Refused (409, `details.reason` variance_exceeded)
when actual cost passes the approved amount by more than the variance
threshold, unless `variance_approved` is sent by someone who can
approve the actual amount. Closing resets the vehicle's PMS intervals.

AllocatePaymentRequest.description: Applying a payment's credit: the invoices and amounts, or nothing (oldest due first).
AllocatePaymentRequest.title: AllocatePaymentRequest

detailer_ids.description: Empty is refused by the engine, in the source's words.

BankReconciliationRequest.description:
Bank reconciliation writes. Opening one: the account, the statement's
closing date and its closing balance in centavos (negative when overdrawn).

BankReconciliationRequest.title: BankReconciliationRequest

BlockSlotsRequest.description: Close slots of one day to new bookings. `slots` are grid slot starts, minutes since midnight.
BlockSlotsRequest.title: BlockSlotsRequest

BookingStatus.description: A booking's lifecycle. The source's values, with `on-going` spelled `on_going`. What each move does to the clock and to the reserved slots is `BookingClock`'s and `SlotRelease`'s.
BookingStatus.title: BookingStatus

ChangeBookingStatusRequest.description:
Move a booking's status. `reason` is kept on a cancellation and logged on
any move; `inspection_override_reason` starts work without the check-in
inspection.
ChangeBookingStatusRequest.title: ChangeBookingStatusRequest

CheckInRequest.description:
GET /check-in/lookup?q=… and POST /check-in (a new customer and vehicle at
the counter).
CheckInRequest.title: CheckInRequest

CheckoutRequest.description: The counter's checkout: how the customer paid. `amount_cents` defaults to everything due.

CloseYearRequest.description: A fiscal (calendar) year: required to close one, optional to look one up.

CrmRequest.description:
Every CRM write and list filter. The CRM's forms are small and share their
field names (a `name`, a `body`, a `template_id`), so one request carries
them all: shape and type here (R3), what a route REQUIRES by its name, and
each route reads the part it needs through a typed accessor.

note.description: Required to decline safety-critical work (checked against the line).

scheduled_date.description: The day and time asked for; `days` is where the work sits.

next.description: What the job is waiting for; the API still checks each step when it is taken.

can_redeem.description: A prepaid credit may settle it instead of an invoice (`POST /crm/prepaid-packages/{id}/redeem`).

DocumentKind.description: Port of ../web's `DocumentKind` and lib/documents.ts / lib/compliance.ts kind sets. Labels are verbatim: alert bodies and the expiring-documents tile print them.

count_unit.description: What the count meter counts: `cups` for the espresso machine, else job `cycles`.

or the Manila date (`due_on`) it falls due at.

due_on.description: The business date it falls on, Asia/Manila (R9).

EquipmentWriteRequest.description:
The small writes against one tool or one package: a status change, a usage
entry, a service entry, a package's equipment profile. Each route reads the
part it needs.

issued_parts.description: Parts the service took from the branch's store.

lines.description: A package's equipment profile: the whole list.

EquipmentWriteRequest.title: EquipmentWriteRequest

needs_reorder.description: At or below its reorder point.

InspectionPhotoRequest.description: A before or after photo: an image, stored like any document (10 MB).
InspectionPhotoRequest.title: InspectionPhotoRequest

tin_printed.description: With the branch code, as an invoice prints it.

non_vat_notice.description: The wording a non-VAT branch's invoice must carry; null for a VAT-registered branch.
enum: THIS DOCUMENT IS NOT VALID FOR CLAIM OF INPUT TAX.

credited_cents.description: Taken off by standing credit notes, and withheld at source on a 2307: they settle the invoice as money does.

IssueCreditNoteRequest.description:
A credit note against an invoice: why, when, and what is credited. A line
names an invoice line (with nothing else: what is left of that line; with a

IssueCreditNoteRequest.title: IssueCreditNoteRequest

IssueInvoiceRequest.description: Issuing: optionally an earlier business date (never in the future, never behind the series).
IssueInvoiceRequest.title: IssueInvoiceRequest

effective_price_cents.description: What a line for this item is priced at in this branch.

ItemType.description: What an item is. A service fee is never stocked.
ItemType.title: ItemType

LeadStage.description: Where a B2B lead stands. The five open stages may be moved between freely (a deal goes backwards as well as forwards). `won` is reached only by converting the lead into a customer account, and is final. `lost` may be re-opened.
LeadStage.title: LeadStage

LineUrgency.description: A safety-critical line cannot be declined without a reason on record.
LineUrgency.title: LineUrgency

selected.description: One branch id, "all" (staff across every allowed branch), or null (portal).

MessagePurpose.description: Why a message is sent, which decides the consent it needs. MessagePurpose.title: MessagePurpose

recorded_by.description: Which staff member recorded it is the shop's business.

MoveType.description: Why stock moved. The sign of a move's quantity says which way; each type says which signs it may carry. - opening      the first count of an item in a location (inbound, costed)  - receipt      goods received against a purchase order (inbound, costed)  - issue        parts issued to a work order (outbound)  - return       the reversal of an issue (inbound) or of a receipt (outbound)  - adjustment   a stock count's variance, either way  - transfer_out / transfer_in   the two halves of one transfer document  - consumption  used up inside the shop (outbound)
MoveType.title: MoveType

PartsSource.description: Where a line's part comes from, per line (the hybrid model). Phase 3's two values keep their meaning and no stock moves for them:  - own_stock          the part is charged, and earns no markup ("the client's  *                       own stock", Shop::partsMargin);  - supplier_provided  the shop buys it in, charged, earning its markup. PayRefundRequest.description:
A refund: the one source it pays out of (a payment's unallocated money, or
a credit note's credit), the method (a reference number unless cash), the
amount (default: everything the source still holds), the business date and

PayRefundRequest.title: PayRefundRequest

PaymentMethod.description: How a payment came in. Everything but cash carries a reference number.
PaymentMethod.title: PaymentMethod

refunded_cents.description: Given back out of what was not allocated (refunds that still stand).

seller.description: What its acknowledgment receipt prints: who received the money, from whom, and what the receipt is not.

prefixItems.const: THIS DOCUMENT IS NOT VALID FOR CLAIM OF INPUT TAX.

PostManualJournalRequest.description:
A journal voucher: the branch it is filed under, its business date, a
reference and memo, and its lines (an account and a debit or a credit in
centavos; a line may sit in another of the caller's branches). Whether it
balances and whether an account may be posted to by hand is the action's.
PostManualJournalRequest.title: PostManualJournalRequest

PublicBookingRequest.description:
A booking request from a branch's public page. The customer says who they
are, what they drive, which package and size, and when; and ticks the
consent to keep their service records, without which no account is opened.
`captcha_token` is checked when the server has a captcha configured.
PublicBookingRequest.title: PublicBookingRequest

RaisePurchaseOrdersRequest.description:
Purchase requests from the forecast: the parts chosen, over the horizon the
forecast was read at. Quantities and prices come from the server's own
forecast, never from here.
RaisePurchaseOrdersRequest.title: RaisePurchaseOrdersRequest

RecordInspectionRequest.description:
A vehicle's inspection at a stage of the booking. A damage point is a place
on the top-down outline, in thousandths of its width (x) and length (y).
RecordInspectionRequest.title: RecordInspectionRequest

RecordPaymentRequest.description:
A payment received: the account, the branch receiving it, the method (a
reference number unless cash), the amount in centavos, the business date it
came in, and optionally how to spread it (else oldest due first).
RecordPaymentRequest.title: RecordPaymentRequest

confirm_warning.description: Required to save a reading the validation flags as unusual.

RecordVendorBillRequest.description:
A vendor's bill: who billed, which branch it is for, the vendor's own
invoice number and dates, how its prices treat VAT, what is withheld at
source, and its lines. Shape only: whether a receipt line can be billed, an
account charged or an invoice number reused is the action's to decide, and

payment.description: Paid on the spot: the cash-out voucher is recorded with the bill.

RecordVendorBillRequest.title: RecordVendorBillRequest

RecordVendorPaymentRequest.description:
A payment to a vendor: the vendor, the branch paying, the method (a
reference number unless cash), the business date, and either the bills it
settles with their amounts or one amount to spread oldest due first.
RecordVendorPaymentRequest.title: RecordVendorPaymentRequest

RecordWithholdingRequest.description:
A BIR 2307 received from a customer: the ATC and rate they withheld at, the
tax base if it is less than the invoice's sales before VAT, the
certificate's own number and period, and the day it was taken off the
invoice. The amount is worked out by the action.
RecordWithholdingRequest.title: RecordWithholdingRequest

RecurringScheduleRequest.description: A customer's standing weekly slot. `day_of_week` is 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday).
RecurringScheduleRequest.title: RecurringScheduleRequest

ReorderRequest.description: The order a branch's packages, categories or add-ons are listed in.
ReorderRequest.title: ReorderRequest

Role.description: Every role a user can hold. The eight ported roles keep the frontend's values, labels and descriptions (golden-tested against rbac.json). `branch_manager` and `cashier` are staff roles new in the API. "Owner" is not a separate role: the owner is a `provider_admin`.
Role.title: Role

registered_name.description:
What this branch's invoices print (Phase 7): its BIR-registered name and
business style, and header / footer text worded by its accountant.

POST creates (with opening consents), PATCH edits. Status changes have their

their own account's contact details and branding, not the shop's commercial
or internal fields.

SaveEquipmentRequest.description:
A tool of the register. On an edit only what is sent changes; a nullable
field sent as null is cleared. Hours are decimals to three places.
SaveEquipmentRequest.title: SaveEquipmentRequest

SaveFleetPartRequest.description:
A customer's spare part. `customer_account_id` (staff; a portal user's own
account otherwise) and `current_stock` are accepted on create only: after
that, stock changes by receiving purchase orders. `usages` replaces the
part's task links when given.
SaveFleetPartRequest.title: SaveFleetPartRequest

SaveInvoiceRequest.description:
Raising a draft (POST): `work_order_ids` (closed jobs of one account), or
a typed-in invoice (`customer_account_id`, `branch_id`, `lines`). Editing a
draft (PATCH): `notes`, a typed-in invoice's `lines`, and `discounts` on any.

SavePackageRequest.description: A package with its price per size class and, optionally, its bill of materials (the whole list).
SavePackageRequest.title: SavePackageRequest

POST registers a vehicle with its first odometer reading (and any known
service history); PATCH edits details. The odometer never changes here
(POST …/readings), nor the owner (POST …/transfer).
SaveVehicleRequest.title: SaveVehicleRequest

registered_name.description: What a bill, a 2307 and the summary list of purchases print (Phase 12).

default_atc_code.description: The tax usually withheld from this vendor: both, or neither.

SaveWorkOrderRequest.description:

SaveWorkOrderRequest.title: SaveWorkOrderRequest

SizeClass.title: SizeClass

StockReasonRequest.description: Cancelling a purchase order, voiding a goods receipt: the reason is required and kept.
StockReasonRequest.title: StockReasonRequest

| | `stock_transfer`

TakeBookingRequest.description:
Take a booking for one of the shop's customers. The plan, the price and the
heads are the API's: the request says who, what, which size, and when.
TakeBookingRequest.title: TakeBookingRequest

TaxClass.description: How an item is taxed (carried for invoicing; Phase 3 billing applies one VAT rate to the order).
TaxClass.title: TaxClass

UpdateBookingRequest.description: A booking's bay, notes, contact details and vehicle: only what is sent changes.
UpdateBookingRequest.title: UpdateBookingRequest

branch_ids.description: [] = every branch (only an unrestricted granter may give that).

multipart/form-data: `file` plus metadata. Name a `vehicle_id` (the
document is filed under the vehicle's current owner) or a

km_remaining.description: For the list's progress meter: km left (negative = past) and the interval used.

VoidDocumentRequest.title: VoidDocumentRequest

WorkOrderLinesRequest.description: PUT /work-orders/{id}/lines (recordLines): the draft's full line list.
WorkOrderLinesRequest.title: WorkOrderLinesRequest

cancel. Each route uses the rules for its own step (route name suffix).
